title: Joseph's dream (Matthew 1:18–25)
hookLine: a quiet carpenter plans to leave quietly, then a dream tells him to stay

lines: THE OTHER SIDE OF THE STORY.
cards: A carpenter in a small town learns that the woman he's promised to is pregnant, and he knows the child isn't his. That's Joseph.

After three days with Mary, all from Luke, Matthew's Gospel tells the same beginning from his side. In those days an engagement was almost a marriage: ending it took a divorce. Picture him that night.
Everyone in a village that size will know soon. He could make it public, and let the whole village judge her. Matthew says Joseph is a just man, and he decides on something else.
He'll end it quietly. No scene, no accusations. He has it all planned.

teach.b: Matthew says he was "minded to put her away privily." Privily means privately. It's already a kind act: he's protecting her even while he's hurt.
But in the night, an angel comes to him in a dream: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
The child's name will be Jesus, a name that means God saves. And Matthew adds an old line from the prophet Isaiah, about a child whose name is Emmanuel, "which being interpreted is, God with us."

Matthew, like Luke, says Jesus had no human father, and he tells it through Joseph's dream. "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife." No argument.
Joseph never says a single word in the Bible. He only listens and acts. He'll have more dreams in Matthew, and each time, he gets up and goes.
He takes a child who isn't his by blood, names him, and raises him as his son, and that naming made Jesus a son of David's family line.
Catholics call him the patron of the whole Church and keep his feast on March nineteenth. The Orthodox remember him as Joseph the Betrothed, soon after Christmas.
Many Protestants hold him up as a picture of quiet, faithful fatherhood. A man who could have walked away, and nobody would have blamed him. He stayed.

how: Catholics keep the Feast of Saint Joseph on March 19, and many honor him as patron of fathers, workers and the whole Church; the Orthodox remember him as Joseph the Betrothed in the days after Christmas.

games.q: you're Joseph. you've decided to end the engagement quietly. then, in a dream, an angel says: fear not to take Mary as your wife. you wake up. what do you do?
o: stick to your plan. it was only a dream.
take Mary as your wife, as the angel said.
ask for a second sign before you decide.
games.why: he wakes up and does exactly what the angel said. no speech, no argument. he names the child Jesus.

practice: Think of one kind thing you could skip today and nobody would blame you: the dishes someone else left, the text you could leave unanswered, the call to the relative who's hard work, the extra minute with someone who's lonely.
Just picture yourself doing it quietly, without telling anyone. If you pray, you can ask for Joseph's kind of steadiness; if you don't, just let the picture settle.

wordCard.voice: Joseph's dream. A just man planning to leave quietly, told in the night: fear not. He woke up and stayed.

carryVoice: Your line: the quiet ones matter. Joseph's story has no lines, only choices. Forty days, done.
